Hello Graziella:

The Wyoming Game and Fish Department is using aerial line transect sampling to estimate abundance of pronghorn in most management units (i.e., populations) across the state. Our application of distance sampling may not be directly comparable to terrestrial surveys of ungulates in forested habitats because pronghorn occupy open habitats and are relatively amenable to aerial surveys.

We started using our technique for pronghorn management in the late 1980's when TRANSECT was the analysis program and have worked up through the various versions of Distance. We just started using the newest Windows version, Distance 3.5, release 5.

We conduct surveys from fixed-wing aircraft where the wing struts and windows have been specifically marked to denote prescribed perpendicular ground distance intervals when the plane is flown at the appropriate height. Onboard computers capture the actual height of the plane above ground level using radar (or laser) altimeters in order to adjust distance bands for the actual height above ground level. Some fairly strict procedures are required to address the assumptions of the technique. To some degree, the protocol we use constrains the type of analyses we perform using Distance. The analysis we run is for clustered populations using perpendicular distances grouped into intervals. We prepared a manual that describes our procedures and basic analyses using Distance 2.2.

For terrestrial surveys, there are other options for obtaining accurate distance data (e.g., laser rangefinders) than the approach we use. Please let me know if I can answer any other questions regarding our use of distance sampling and analysis using Distance.

Good luck!
